subject.title: [Tooling]: Add pre/post-update compatibility scanner with risk report and smoke recommendations

question: Should OpenClaw define a first-class `doctor --upgrade-scan` or update-integrated upgrade assessment contract, and what JSON schema, redaction rules, smoke-check boundaries, and rollback-hint semantics should it expose?
rationale: The missing work is a public tooling/report contract with security, compatibility, operator-action, and automation implications, not a narrow code defect automation can safely choose alone.

options.title: Design Core Upgrade Assessment
options.body: Define a core-owned scanner/report contract that composes existing doctor, update, plugin, health, backup, and rollback surfaces without duplicating validators.

options.title: Keep Existing Adjacent Pieces
options.body: Treat doctor lint and plugin post-upgrade probes as sufficient for now, accepting that unified risk scoring and rollback guidance remain absent.

options.title: Defer To External Automation
options.body: Leave this as an external script or skill, avoiding a core API commitment but leaving missing core upgrade/report contracts unresolved.

recommendation.title: Design Core Upgrade Assessment
recommendation.body: Define a core-owned scanner/report contract that composes existing doctor, update, plugin, health, backup, and rollback surfaces without duplicating validators.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest observed connection across the prior review, current-main blame, update safety work, and the closest merged post-upgrade subset.
